minor_characters.name: Catherine
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Myrtle Wilson’s sister at the Manhattan apartment party; later lies to the coroner at the inquest.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her gossip and later perjury add color but do not affect Tom’s affair, Myrtle’s death, or Wilson’s revenge as preserved in the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: Chester McKee
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A would‑be photographer at Myrtle’s party, seen drunkenly in the apartment and in a brief elevator scene with Nick.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is comic texture only and cutting him doesn’t change Nick’s exposure to Tom and Myrtle’s tawdry world.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. McKee
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chester’s shrill, languid wife who flits through the apartment gathering and praises Myrtle’s dress.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her presence is atmospheric and has no bearing on any later event or character arc.

minor_characters.name: Ewing Klipspringer
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Gatsby’s perennial houseguest who plays the piano during Daisy’s first visit and later phones only to ask for his tennis shoes.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Gatsby’s social emptiness at the end is already clear from the empty funeral and can be shown without this character.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Sloane
minor_characters.appearances_summary: An aloof East Egger on horseback who pointedly snubs Gatsby during an impromptu call with Tom.
minor_characters.reason_removable: East Egg disdain is established by Tom’s behavior at Gatsby’s party and in the Plaza showdown without needing Sloane by name.

minor_characters.name: Lucille
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One of the ‘girls in yellow’ at Gatsby’s party who spreads fanciful rumors and anecdotes about him.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her lines can be folded into the general rumor‑mill the synopsis already assumes around Gatsby’s parties.

minor_characters.name: Miss Baedeker
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A tipsy partygoer at Gatsby’s who causes a small comic scene about being dunked in a pool.
minor_characters.reason_removable: She contributes only comic business and has no causal role in the plot.

minor_characters.name: Slagle
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The Chicago caller after Gatsby’s death who mentions Young Parke and bad bonds.
minor_characters.reason_removable: This one‑off name only reiterates criminal ties already covered by Wolfshiem and can be dropped.

minor_characters.name: "Blocks" Biloxi
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A name in Daisy and Jordan’s humorous digression about someone fainting at Daisy’s wedding.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He exists solely inside a comic anecdote that doesn’t affect the Plaza confrontation’s outcome.

minor_characters.name: Stella
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Meyer Wolfshiem’s office assistant who screens Nick at the door.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her gatekeeping is incidental to Wolfshiem’s refusal to ‘get mixed up’ and can be omitted.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Sigourney Howard
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Jordan Baker’s aunt, mentioned as the name under which Jordan can be reached.
minor_characters.reason_removable: She’s a name in a phone book and has no effect on Nick and Jordan’s relationship arc.

minor_characters.name: Pammy Buchanan
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Daisy and Tom’s young daughter, briefly brought in to meet Gatsby.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her cameo can be cut without altering the affair, the Plaza confrontation, or the fallout summarized in the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: Ferdie
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Daisy’s chauffeur briefly named when she arrives for tea at Nick’s cottage.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A one‑line helper whose name adds nothing to plot or theme.

minor_characters.name: Michaelis
minor_characters.appearances_summary: The Greek coffee‑shop owner who narrates Wilson’s state after Myrtle’s death.
minor_characters.reason_removable: His eyewitness account can be summarized or omitted since the synopsis attributes Wilson’s actions to grief and Tom’s prompting.

subplots.name: Nick’s supposed engagement and back‑home ‘entanglement’
subplots.reason_removable: This offstage rumor and letter‑writing do not affect Nick’s role as observer or any event in the Long Island summer.

subplots.name: Nick’s brief Jersey City office romance
subplots.reason_removable: A throwaway liaison that neither shapes his arc with Jordan nor touches the central plot.

subplots.name: Jordan’s golf‑cheating scandal and the ‘bad driver’ talk
subplots.reason_removable: Her cool dishonesty can be implied in fewer strokes, and Nick’s later break with her stands without this sporting backstory.

subplots.name: Rosy Rosenthal murder reminiscence at the Metropole
subplots.reason_removable: It’s atmospheric color around Wolfshiem; the necessary point—that he’s a gambler tied to Gatsby—remains without it.

subplots.name: Owl‑Eyes’s car‑ditch fiasco after the party
subplots.reason_removable: A comic capper to a party that can be dropped without changing the legend of Gatsby’s gatherings.

subplots.name: Klipspringer’s ‘tennis shoes’ phone call
subplots.reason_removable: Gatsby’s lonely funeral is already conveyed by the fact that only Owl‑Eyes and his father attend.

subplots.name: The police stop and the commissioner’s Christmas card
subplots.reason_removable: A flourish of Gatsby’s pull that’s redundant once Wolfshiem and the bootlegging are established.

subplots.name: Michaelis’s all‑night vigil and Wilson’s step‑by‑step movements
subplots.reason_removable: These procedural beats can be compressed into the synopsis’s simpler chain of causation.

subplots.name: Slagle’s Chicago call about ‘Young Parke’ and counterfeit bonds
subplots.reason_removable: A posthumous criminal aside that adds nothing essential to the plot or to Gatsby’s already‑implied illegality.

digressions.topic: The multi‑paragraph roll call of Gatsby’s weekend guests by name and pedigree
digressions.reason_removable: A catalogic flourish that can be replaced by a brief sentence about uninvited crowds without losing any plot or theme.

digressions.topic: Nick’s Carraway family pedigree (Dukes of Buccleuch, great‑uncle, Civil War substitute) and clan pride
digressions.reason_removable: Genealogical color isn’t required by the synopsis’s framing of Nick as a Midwesterner who comes East to learn bonds.

digressions.topic: Daisy’s ‘butler’s nose’ anecdote during the first dinner
digressions.reason_removable: A comic aside with no consequences for plot or character.

digressions.topic: Nick’s essayistic reverie on his work routines, Yale Club dinners, Fifth Avenue fantasies, and metropolitan loneliness
digressions.reason_removable: Atmospheric meditation that does not bear on the preserved events or decisions.

digressions.topic: The long ‘Blocks Biloxi’ wedding‑day detour in the Plaza scene
digressions.reason_removable: Comic embroidery that can be excised without touching the confrontation between Gatsby, Daisy, and Tom.

digressions.topic: Nick’s Midwestern Christmas‑train nostalgia and Union Station vignette before his decision to return home
digressions.reason_removable: His resolution to leave the East (and the closing New World meditation) stands without this extended reminiscence.
